learning_outcomes.text: To solve problems with initiative, decision making, creativity, critical thinking and to communicate and transfer knowledge, abilities and skills in the area of Industrial engineering.
To develop modeling and simulation processes in mechanical engineering computer aided design.
To model, simulate and manage mechanical elements by means of CAD/CAE tools.
To create and interpret technical documentation. Technical blue prints for project development and documentation.
Proactively collaborating in the development of work, setting goals and meeting objectives.
Showing initiative to organise one's own work, managing the effort and time devoted to achieving the proposed objectives and goals

syllabus_topics: Parts creation linked to a table.
teaching_methods: Practical classes (team work sessions supervised by the teacher)
Laboratory activities (in spaces with specialized equipment)
Team work (individual and group essay preparation, problem solving)

assessment_methods.method: Observation Synchronous (On-site or via Florida Oberta/Microsoft Teams)
Practical tasks Synchronous (On-site or via Florida Oberta/Microsoft Teams)
Project Synchronous (On-site or via Florida Oberta/Microsoft Teams)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on Observation (15%), Practical tasks (35%), and Project (50%). A minimum grade of 5 points is required to pass the subject. Delayed delivery of practical tasks may result in a reduction of marks between 10% and 50%. AI usage rules are specified across three levels: Level 1 (not permitted, considered plagiarism, penalty up to 0 or course failure for in-person assessments); Level 2 (permitted with simple citation, undeclared use is plagiarism, penalty up to 0); Level 3 (extensive use permitted with full traceability, non-compliance is plagiarism, penalty up to 0).
